reference_title: Pavement Design for Roads, Streets, Walks, and Storage Areas

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.summary: Base courses under rigid pavements replace soft/compressible/expansive soils and add structural strength, uniform bearing, frost protection, drainage, and a stable construction surface (esp. for slip-form paving); use is an economic decision; minimum 4 in over OH/CH/CL/MH/ML/OL subgrades to prevent pumping (SM/SC too, under adverse moisture); never use fines to level/choke open-graded base (pumping risk); positive drainage is required to avoid trapped groundwater.
sections.body: Base courses may be required under rigid pavements for replacing soft, highly compressible or expansive soils and for providing the following: additional structural strength; more uniform bearing surface for the pavement; protection for the subgrade against detrimental frost action; drainage; suitable surface for the operation of construction equipment, especially slip form pavers. Use of base courses under a rigid pavement to provide structural benefit should be based on economy of construction. Thick base courses have often resulted in lower maintenance costs since the thick base course provides stronger foundation and therefore less slab movement. Provide a minimum base-course thickness of 4 in (100 mm) over subgrades that are classified as OH, CH, CL, MH, ML, and OL to provide protection against pumping. In certain cases of adverse moisture conditions (high groundwater table or poor drainage), SM and SC soils also may require base courses to prevent pumping. The designer is cautioned against the use of fine-grained material for leveling courses or choking open-graded base courses since this may create a pumping condition. Positive drainage should be provided for all base courses to ensure groundwater is not trapped directly beneath the pavement since saturation of these layers will cause the pumping condition that the base course is intended to prevent. The base course material and drains must meet the drainage criteria listed in Chapter titled Design of Subsurface Pavement Drainage Systems.
key_points: Minimum 4 in base over OH/CH/CL/MH/ML/OL subgrades for anti-pumping protection.
Never use fines as a leveling/choke course on open-graded base -- creates a pumping condition.
Positive drainage is mandatory to prevent trapped groundwater beneath the slab.
sections.applicability: Deciding whether/how thick a base course is needed under a rigid pavement.

sections.title: Materials
sections.summary: Investigate source/quantity/characteristics; base may be natural, processed, or stabilized, chosen for its intended purpose; all bases under concrete for roads/parking must meet <=85% passing No.10, <=15% passing No.200, PI<=6, plus any locally warranted controls (e.g. abrasion loss).
sections.body: If conditions indicate that a base course is desirable under a rigid pavement, a thorough investigation should be made to determine the source, quantity, and characteristics of the available materials. A study should also be made to determine the most economical thickness of material for a base course that will meet the requirements. The base course may consist of natural, processed, or stabilized materials. The material selected should be the one that best accomplishes the intended purpose of the base course. In general, the base course material should be a well-graded, high-stability material. In this connection, all base courses to be placed beneath concrete pavements for roads and parking areas should conform to the following requirements: percent passing No. 10 sieve: not more than 85; percent passing No. 200 sieve: not more than 15; plasticity index: not higher than 6; where local experience indicates their desirability, other control limitations such as limited abrasion loss may be imposed to ensure a uniform high-quality base course.
key_points: Rigid-pavement base gradation floor: <=85% passing No.10, <=15% passing No.200, PI <= 6.
sections.applicability: Base course material qualification for rigid pavements.

sections.title: Compaction
sections.summary: Compact rigid-pavement base course to a minimum 95% maximum density; thin base on a yielding subgrade is difficult to compact to high density.
sections.body: Where base courses are used under rigid pavements, the base course material should be compacted to a minimum of 95 percent of the maximum density. The engineer is cautioned that it is difficult to compact thin base courses to high densities when they are placed on yielding subgrades.
key_points: Rigid base course compaction floor: 95% max density.

sections.title: Frost Requirements
sections.summary: In seasonal-frost areas, follow Chapter 19's base-course thickness and gradation requirements.
sections.body: In areas where subgrade soils are subjected to seasonal frost action detrimental to the performance of pavements, use the requirements for base course thickness and gradation outlined in Chapter titled Seasonal Frost Conditions.
key_points: Rigid base course thickness/gradation in frost areas is governed by Chapter 19, not this chapter's non-frost requirements.
sections.applicability: Cross-reference to Chapter 19 for frost-area base design.
